posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
I am in need of some red wavelength safelights so that I don't have to use my HeNe lasers as safelights anymore and I was thinking a couple of small Neon lights might do well. They are very inexpensive for the small ones and are readily available on e-bay. 

Has anyone use red Neon lights for safelights and know if their band/bands/bandwidth is contained wholly in the red?

Also, there are blue "Neon" lights out there that I assume are made with Argon gas. I wonder if they can be used for red sensitive emulsion.

I know most emulsion do have some sensitivity to the non sensitive wavelengths and thusly one should not use too high a wattage.

If I can think about it I will take my handy dandy cool diffraction glasses down to the city one night and take a peak at the different color Neon lights to see their sprectral output.

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md:
I use the sheets that disco's use in front of their lamps. I mounted them in front of normal spot lights that people use to couzy their houses. The sheets are designed to withstand the high power of disco lamps, so temperature is not a problem.

You can buy them here: [http://www.leefilters.com/LPFD.asp?PageID=320](http://www.leefilters.com/LPFD.asp?PageID=320)

If you stack two filters, you will have absolutely no light other than red. I have two of these setups, one for red and one for green. With them I can bathe my garage in single colour safe light.

posts.author: ron olson
posts.content_md:
John,

Use red or amber LED's from OptiLED instead of bothering with neon or filtered white light. TheLED's run ~$40 each and are available through our web site [http://www.laserreflections.com](http://www.laserreflections.com). In my darkroom I have five 2W LED's and they allow great visibility.

You can hang the disco sheets in front of a 100W light bulb and not worry about any other colours coming through. Als, you can use a standard dimmer if you get blinded by your red safe light. I have used the green one with my pfg-01 film and MBDCG. I even let the film settle with the disco safe light on. Some times for one hour. No problem. I use the red light with normal dcg also no problem. I bought the sheets here in Holland in a package of 4 basic colours (blue, green, yellow and red). They cost me about 15 Euro.

posts.author: Hans
posts.content_md:
The sheets that I can buy here are not so large. They are about legal letter size and come in a package of 4 colours. The (106) primary red is included. With one sheet I can make one safe light because I cut them in half and then stack them in front of the safe light.

They also make a great substitute for laser safety glasses. I just painted a pair of chemical protection glasses black on the sides and glued red sheet in front of it. I now have safety glasses (for my C315M) for a fraction of the cost from when I have to order them.

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
> **Colin Kaminski:** [Are you able to use the Amber Optileds with he Fuji film?

I finally did a safelight test and found that there was still some sensitivity to the Optiled amber LEDs with Fuji film. They are useable, but to avoid any fogging it's best to use the minimum possible light levels and exposure times and, for an area safelight, to shield the setup from the safelight if it's sitting there for a prolonged settling time.

Another yellow LED I tried (extracted from a solar garden light) was much worse - it was more yellow than the amber LED and the film was considerably more sensitive to it.
